Part Two Parents and/or Family

Article 68

The family in efforts to Protect women's rights plays a role in:

a. protecting women and children from conflict and domestic Violence that degrades human dignity;

b. providing equal opportunities for women and children to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural affairs; and

c. preventing violations of the rights of women and children in the household.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. City is the City of Prabumulih. 2. City Government is the Government of the City of Prabumulih. 3. Mayor is the Mayor of the City of Prabumulih. 4. Vice Mayor is the Vice Mayor of the City of Prabumulih. 5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of the City of Prabumulih

6. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of the City of Prabumulih. 7. Office of Population Control Family Planning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPKBPPPA is the Office of Population Control Family Planning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of the City of Prabumulih. 8. Regional General Hospital hereinafter abbreviated as RSUD is the Regional General Hospital RSUD of the City of Prabumulih

9. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is the Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of the City of Prabumulih

10. Community-Based Integrated Protection hereinafter abbreviated as PATBM is the Community-Based Integrated Protection PATBM of the City of Prabumulih

11. Community Health Center hereinafter abbreviated as Puskesmas is the Community Health Center Puskesmas of the City of Prabumulih

12. Regional Technical Implementation Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD is the Technical Implementation element of the Office that carries out Technical Operational activities and/or certain Technical Supporting Activities; 13. Private Sector is part of the economy outside Government ownership, consisting of Individuals or groups of Individuals with Legal Entity that carry out Public services in the City of Prabumulih

14. Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improvement of quality of life, and enhancement of women's participation in development. 15. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 16. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb and is not married. 17. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 18. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 19. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 20. Child-Friendly City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a City that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights

21. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the Region. 22. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 23. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 24. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 25. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 26. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 27. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 28. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 29. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that is gender sensitive. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 31. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 32.

Part Two Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women and Children

Article 17

In order to prevent acts of Violence against women and children, the City Government:

a. conducts socialization regarding the prevention of Violence against women and children by optimizing the role of customary institutions, Education, culture, religion and community organizations;

b. builds networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, universities and various non-governmental organizations that work and/or care for women and children victims of Violence;

c. provides public facilities that are comfortable and safe for women and children; and

d. establishes an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment P2TP2A formed by decree of the Mayor and provides a Secretariat for the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment.

Article 30

(1) Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women and children victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

(2) Social reintegration is intended so that:

a. women and children victims of acts of Violence can resume their social life; and

b. women and children victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life.

(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

Part Five Law Enforcement and Legal Aid

Article 27

(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 19 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in the context of handling cases of acts of Violence against women and children, especially to provide sanctions against perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 25

(1) The City Government may provide safe houses for women and children victims of acts of Violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and children victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for women and children victims of acts of Violence who require a safe house include:

a. their life is threatened;

b. receiving rejection from family or community;

c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or

d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have sensitivity to women's empowerment and child protection and/or gender awareness, consisting of:

a. social workers/volunteers;

b. security officers; and/or

c. community leaders.

(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

CHAPTER X SANCTIONS

Article 73

(1) Any person who deliberately fails to provide protection to women and Children resulting in violence, fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

(2) If an official appointed to provide protection fails to carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

(3) UPT managers who carry out service duties but violate service principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable mechanism.

(4) Private parties that carry out Public services and fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities in accordance with this regulation shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 21

(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of:

a. victims;

b. families;

c. communities; and/or

d. community organizations in the field of Protection of women and children.

(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:

a. directly;

b. by telephone; and/or

c. by letter.

(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency responsible for the Protection of Women and children, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20, are also authorized to conduct Assistance in handling victims of acts of Violence against women and children obtained through other information.

(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Part Three Health Rehabilitation

Article 22

(1) Health rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter b constitutes efforts that include aspects of:

a. promotive;

b. preventive;

c. curative; and

d. rehabilitative.

(2) Health rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours, of quality and conducted in accordance with health service standards.

(3) Women and children victims of acts of Violence and children in conflict with the law have the right to health services free of charge, including:

a. medical services;

b. medicolegal services;

c. psychosocial counseling; and

d. visum.

(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementing health services as referred to in paragraph (3) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 31

The City Government implements repatriation and social reintegration of women and children victims of acts of Violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

Part Four Health and Social

Article 48

(1) The City Government is required to organize comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the womb.

(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services; and

b. exemption from cost burdens for Children with malnutrition, Children with disabilities, Children with special needs, Children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, Children victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, Children who are victims of Violence, and Children victims of human trafficking.

(3) The City Government, community, family and parents are required to ensure that Children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Article 65

Service efforts carried out by the City Government for child victims of acts of Violence as referred to in Article 42 through Article 64 shall apply mutatis mutandis to service efforts for child victims of acts of Violence.

Part Six Repatriation and Social Reintegration

Article 29

(1) Repatriation is intended to return women and children victims of acts of Violence to their region of origin.

(2) Repatriation of women and children victims of acts of violence is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

Article 46

(1) Every Child has the right to obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.

(2) Every Child has the right to receive Protection in education units from sexual crimes and Violence committed by educators, education personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.

CHAPTER VII COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION, AND PARENTS AND/OR FAMILY

Part One Community

Article 66

(1) Community participation in efforts to Protect women and Children:

a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and Children;

b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and Children to the competent authorities; and

c. supervise the law enforcement process for cases of violations of the rights of women and Children.

(2) The community, parents and family are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and Children.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

c. community leaders.

(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Part Two Parents and/or Family

Article 68

The family in efforts to Protect women's rights plays a role in:

a. protecting women and children from conflict and domestic Violence that degrades human dignity;

b. providing equal opportunities for women and children to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural affairs; and

c. preventing violations of the rights of women and children in the household.

Part Four Health and Social

Article 48

(1) The City Government is required to organize comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the womb.

(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services; and

b. exemption from cost burdens for Children with malnutrition, Children with disabilities, Children with special needs, Children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, Children victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, Children who are victims of Violence, and Children victims of human trafficking.

(3) The City Government, community, family and parents are required to ensure that Children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Article 21

(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of:

a. victims;

b. families;

c. communities; and/or

d. community organizations in the field of Protection of women and children.

(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:

a. directly;

b. by telephone; and/or

c. by letter.

(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency responsible for the Protection of Women and children, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20, are also authorized to conduct Assistance in handling victims of acts of Violence against women and children obtained through other information.

(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Part Two Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women and Children

Article 17

In order to prevent acts of Violence against women and children, the City Government:

a. conducts socialization regarding the prevention of Violence against women and children by optimizing the role of customary institutions, Education, culture, religion and community organizations;

b. builds networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, universities and various non-governmental organizations that work and/or care for women and children victims of Violence;

c. provides public facilities that are comfortable and safe for women and children; and

d. establishes an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment P2TP2A formed by decree of the Mayor and provides a Secretariat for the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment.

Article 45

(1) Every organizer of an education unit is required to provide opportunities for Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.

(2) Every organizer of an education unit is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.

(3) In the event that a Child victim of Violence experiences dropping out of school, the organizer of the education unit must coordinate with relevant agencies.

Article 31

The City Government implements repatriation and social reintegration of women and children victims of acts of Violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

Part Six Repatriation and Social Reintegration

Article 29

(1) Repatriation is intended to return women and children victims of acts of Violence to their region of origin.

(2) Repatriation of women and children victims of acts of violence is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

Part Five Law Enforcement and Legal Aid

Article 27

(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 19 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in the context of handling cases of acts of Violence against women and children, especially to provide sanctions against perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

a. promotive;

b. preventive;

c. curative; and

d. rehabilitative.

(2) Health rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours, of quality and conducted in accordance with health service standards.

(3) Women and children victims of acts of Violence and children in conflict with the law have the right to health services free of charge, including:

a. medical services;

(1) Every Child has the right to obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.

IMPROVEMENT OF QUALITY OF LIFE OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part One

General

Article 5

(1) In order to improve the quality of life of women and children, the City Government is responsible for:

a. respecting and guaranteeing the rights of women and children without discrimination in accordance with human dignity;

b. enhancing Women's Empowerment and child protection in terms of role, quality and capacity in the fields of:

1. politics;

2. law;

3. social;

4. economy; and

5. culture.

c. strengthening and developing service provider institutions for Women's Empowerment and child protection in the City.

(2) The responsibility of the City Government in efforts to improve the quality of life of women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by Regional Apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.

(2) The community, parents and family are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and Children.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 17

In order to prevent acts of Violence against women and children, the City Government:

a. conducts socialization regarding the prevention of Violence against women and children by optimizing the role of customary institutions, Education, culture, religion and community organizations;

b. builds networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, universities and various non-governmental organizations that work and/or care for women and children victims of Violence;

c. provides public facilities that are comfortable and safe for women and children; and

d. establishes an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment P2TP2A formed by decree of the Mayor and provides a Secretariat for the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment.

Article 71

(1) Supervision of the implementation of women's empowerment and Child Protection as regulated in this Regional Regulation is carried out by a Supervisory institution specifically established for that purpose.

(2) In carrying out supervision, the Institution referred to is authorized to recommend cases to law enforcement officials, government agencies and other community institutions as regulated in the Law.

(3) Recommendations submitted must be followed up by law enforcement officials, government agencies, community institutions and other related individuals.

CHAPTER II

IMPROVEMENT OF QUALITY OF LIFE OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part One

General

Article 5

(1) In order to improve the quality of life of women and children, the City Government is responsible for:

a. respecting and guaranteeing the rights of women and children without discrimination in accordance with human dignity;

b. enhancing Women's Empowerment and child protection in terms of role, quality and capacity in the fields of:

1. politics;

2. law;

3. social;

4. economy; and

5. culture.

c. strengthening and developing service provider institutions for Women's Empowerment and child protection in the City.

(2) The responsibility of the City Government in efforts to improve the quality of life of women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by Regional Apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.

Article 46

(1) Every Child has the right to obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.

(2) Every Child has the right to receive Protection in education units from sexual crimes and Violence committed by educators, education personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.

Article 21

(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of:

a. victims;

b. families;

c. communities; and/or

d. community organizations in the field of Protection of women and children.

(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:

a. directly;

b. by telephone; and/or

c. by letter.

(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency responsible for the Protection of Women and children, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20, are also authorized to conduct Assistance in handling victims of acts of Violence against women and children obtained through other information.

(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Part Three Health Rehabilitation

Article 22

(1) Health rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter b constitutes efforts that include aspects of:

a. promotive;

b. preventive;

c. curative; and

d. rehabilitative.

(2) Health rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours, of quality and conducted in accordance with health service standards.

(3) Women and children victims of acts of Violence and children in conflict with the law have the right to health services free of charge, including:

a. medical services;

b. medicolegal services;

c. psychosocial counseling; and

d. visum.

(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementing health services as referred to in paragraph (3) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 26

(1) Spiritual guidance aims for psychological recovery.

(2) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principles of:

a. not imposing any religion or belief; and

b. leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim (self determination).

(3) Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual guidance officers.

(4) Spiritual guidance officers as referred to in paragraph (3) consist of consultants from the Marriage Advisory, Development and Preservation Agency (BP4), Officers of the Religious Affairs Office, Ustads/Ulamas, Priests, Pastors and other religious leaders who have sensitivity to women's empowerment and child protection and/or gender awareness.

Part Five Law Enforcement and Legal Aid

Article 27

(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 19 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in the context of handling cases of acts of Violence against women and children, especially to provide sanctions against perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

CHAPTER X SANCTIONS

Article 73

(1) Any person who deliberately fails to provide protection to women and Children resulting in violence, fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

(2) If an official appointed to provide protection fails to carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

(3) UPT managers who carry out service duties but violate service principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable mechanism.

(4) Private parties that carry out Public services and fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities in accordance with this regulation shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

Part Two Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women and Children

Article 17

In order to prevent acts of Violence against women and children, the City Government:

a. conducts socialization regarding the prevention of Violence against women and children by optimizing the role of customary institutions, Education, culture, religion and community organizations;

b. builds networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, universities and various non-governmental organizations that work and/or care for women and children victims of Violence;

c. provides public facilities that are comfortable and safe for women and children; and

d. establishes an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment P2TP2A formed by decree of the Mayor and provides a Secretariat for the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment.

Article 27

(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 19 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in the context of handling cases of acts of Violence against women and children, especially to provide sanctions against perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 21

(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of:

a. victims;

b. families;

c. communities; and/or

d. community organizations in the field of Protection of women and children.

(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:

a. directly;

b. by telephone; and/or

c. by letter.

(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency responsible for the Protection of Women and children, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20, are also authorized to conduct Assistance in handling victims of acts of Violence against women and children obtained through other information.

(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 30

(1) Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women and children victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

(2) Social reintegration is intended so that:

a. women and children victims of acts of Violence can resume their social life; and

b. women and children victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life.

(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

a. promotive;

b. preventive;

c. curative; and

d. rehabilitative.

a. medical services;

b. medicolegal services;

c. psychosocial counseling; and

d. visum.

Article 25

(1) The City Government may provide safe houses for women and children victims of acts of Violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and children victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for women and children victims of acts of Violence who require a safe house include:

a. their life is threatened;

b. receiving rejection from family or community;

c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or

d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

a. social workers/volunteers;

b. security officers; and/or

c. community leaders.

(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

CHAPTER VII COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION, AND PARENTS AND/OR FAMILY

Part One Community

Article 66

(1) Community participation in efforts to Protect women and Children:

a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and Children;

b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and Children to the competent authorities; and

c. supervise the law enforcement process for cases of violations of the rights of women and Children.

(2) The community, parents and family are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and Children.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 67

(1) In order to prevent violations of women's rights, the community:

a. monitors various conditions occurring in their environment that may lead to violations of women's rights;

b. increases awareness of violations of women's rights;

c. strengthens the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and

d. supervises the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection organized by the City Government

through a mechanism for conveying aspirations to the Mayor or the Regional House of Representatives.

(2) In order to prevent violations of Children's rights, the community:

a. monitors various conditions occurring in their environment that lead to violations of Children's rights;

b. increases awareness of violations of Children's rights; and

c. strengthens the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and prevents early marriage.

Part Six Facilitation of the Juvenile Justice System

Article 58

(1) Facilitation of the juvenile justice system includes criminal and civil justice.

(2) Facilitation of the criminal justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:

a. provision of companions or Child volunteers during examination by investigators;

b. provision of legal aid and psychologist services;

c. involving members/investigators of the local police in efforts to prevent criminal acts committed by Children as well as Children as victims;

d. realizing a restorative justice process for Children in conflict with the law; and

e. rehabilitation and social reintegration services.

(3) Fulfillment of Children's rights in the civil justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) includes the provision and delivery of consultation and legal aid services during the judicial process.

(4) In facilitating the juvenile justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), the authorized RG is the RG with authority over women and Child empowerment and Protection and has the obligation to accompany child victims and perpetrators in police, prosecution and court examinations.

Part Two Parents and/or Family

Article 68

The family in efforts to Protect women's rights plays a role in:

a. protecting women and children from conflict and domestic Violence that degrades human dignity;

b. providing equal opportunities for women and children to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural affairs; and

c. preventing violations of the rights of women and children in the household.

Article 31

The City Government implements repatriation and social reintegration of women and children victims of acts of Violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

Article 48

(1) The City Government is required to organize comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the womb.

(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services; and

b. exemption from cost burdens for Children with malnutrition, Children with disabilities, Children with special needs, Children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, Children victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, Children who are victims of Violence, and Children victims of human trafficking.

Article 57

(1) Every person/entity is prohibited from employing and involving Children in the worst forms of work.

c. all work that utilizes, provides, or involves Children for the production and trade of alcoholic beverages, narcotics, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances; and/or

d. all work that endangers the health, safety, or morals of Children.

With Mutual Approval of THE REGIONAL HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES OF PRABUMULIH CITY and THE MAYOR OF PRABUMULIH DECIDE:

To Establish : REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION. CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 25

(1) The City Government may provide safe houses for women and children victims of acts of Violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and children victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for women and children victims of acts of Violence who require a safe house include:

a. their life is threatened;

b. receiving rejection from family or community;

c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or

d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have sensitivity to women's empowerment and child protection and/or gender awareness, consisting of:

a. social workers/volunteers;

b. security officers; and/or

c. community leaders.

(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 30

(1) Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women and children victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

(2) Social reintegration is intended so that:

a. women and children victims of acts of Violence can resume their social life; and

b. women and children victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life.

(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

Part Six Facilitation of the Juvenile Justice System

Article 58

(1) Facilitation of the juvenile justice system includes criminal and civil justice.

(2) Facilitation of the criminal justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:

a. provision of companions or Child volunteers during examination by investigators;

b. provision of legal aid and psychologist services;

c. involving members/investigators of the local police in efforts to prevent criminal acts committed by Children as well as Children as victims;

d. realizing a restorative justice process for Children in conflict with the law; and

e. rehabilitation and social reintegration services.

(3) Fulfillment of Children's rights in the civil justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) includes the provision and delivery of consultation and legal aid services during the judicial process.

(4) In facilitating the juvenile justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), the authorized RG is the RG with authority over women and Child empowerment and Protection and has the obligation to accompany child victims and perpetrators in police, prosecution and court examinations.

CHAPTER II

Part One

General

Article 5

(1) In order to improve the quality of life of women and children, the City Government is responsible for:

a. respecting and guaranteeing the rights of women and children without discrimination in accordance with human dignity;

b. enhancing Women's Empowerment and child protection in terms of role, quality and capacity in the fields of:

1. politics;

2. law;

3. social;

4. economy; and

5. culture.

c. strengthening and developing service provider institutions for Women's Empowerment and child protection in the City.

(2) The responsibility of the City Government in efforts to improve the quality of life of women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by Regional Apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.

Article 67

(1) In order to prevent violations of women's rights, the community:

a. monitors various conditions occurring in their environment that may lead to violations of women's rights;

b. increases awareness of violations of women's rights;

c. strengthens the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and

d. supervises the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection organized by the City Government

through a mechanism for conveying aspirations to the Mayor or the Regional House of Representatives.

(2) In order to prevent violations of Children's rights, the community:

a. monitors various conditions occurring in their environment that lead to violations of Children's rights;

b. increases awareness of violations of Children's rights; and

c. strengthens the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and prevents early marriage.

Part Two Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women and Children

Article 17

In order to prevent acts of Violence against women and children, the City Government:

a. conducts socialization regarding the prevention of Violence against women and children by optimizing the role of customary institutions, Education, culture, religion and community organizations;

b. builds networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, universities and various non-governmental organizations that work and/or care for women and children victims of Violence;

c. provides public facilities that are comfortable and safe for women and children; and

d. establishes an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment P2TP2A formed by decree of the Mayor and provides a Secretariat for the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment.

CHAPTER X SANCTIONS

Article 73

(1) Any person who deliberately fails to provide protection to women and Children resulting in violence, fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

(2) If an official appointed to provide protection fails to carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

(3) UPT managers who carry out service duties but violate service principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable mechanism.

(4) Private parties that carry out Public services and fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities in accordance with this regulation shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 71

(1) Supervision of the implementation of women's empowerment and Child Protection as regulated in this Regional Regulation is carried out by a Supervisory institution specifically established for that purpose.

(2) In carrying out supervision, the Institution referred to is authorized to recommend cases to law enforcement officials, government agencies and other community institutions as regulated in the Law.

(3) Recommendations submitted must be followed up by law enforcement officials, government agencies, community institutions and other related individuals.

Article 26

(1) Spiritual guidance aims for psychological recovery.

(2) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principles of:

a. not imposing any religion or belief; and

b. leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim (self determination).

(3) Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual guidance officers.

(4) Spiritual guidance officers as referred to in paragraph (3) consist of consultants from the Marriage Advisory, Development and Preservation Agency (BP4), Officers of the Religious Affairs Office, Ustads/Ulamas, Priests, Pastors and other religious leaders who have sensitivity to women's empowerment and child protection and/or gender awareness.

Part Three  Establishment of Working Group  for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the City

Article 8

(1) In an effort to accelerate the institutionalization of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in all Regional Apparatus, a working group for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the City shall be established.

(2) Members of the working group for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are all heads/leaders of Regional Apparatus.

(3) The Mayor shall appoint the Head of the Regional Apparatus that handles Women's Empowerment duties as Chairman of the Working Group and Head of the Secretariat of the Regional Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Working Group.

(4) The establishment of the City Women's Empowerment and Child Protection working group shall be stipulated by Mayor's Decree.

Part Two Parents and/or Family

Article 68

The family in efforts to Protect women's rights plays a role in:

a. protecting women and children from conflict and domestic Violence that degrades human dignity;

b. providing equal opportunities for women and children to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural affairs; and

c. preventing violations of the rights of women and children in the household.

Part Five Law Enforcement and Legal Aid

Article 27

(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 19 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in the context of handling cases of acts of Violence against women and children, especially to provide sanctions against perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

CHAPTER IX FINANCING

Article 72

Financing for the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection programs and activities is sourced from:

a. regional revenue and expenditure budget; and

b. other legitimate sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 15

Efforts to enhance the role, quality and capability of women in the economic sector as referred to in Article 5 paragraph (1) letter b number 4 include:

a. implementing programs, activities, training for the enhancement of women's skills and expertise in order to realize the improvement of women's welfare;

b. facilitation of business capital strengthening for women with weak economies;

c. marketing of products from businesses of women with weak economies; d. training for the development of women's capabilities through economic empowerment of pre-prosperous families; and

e. comprehensive entrepreneurship training for women.

Article 45

(1) Every organizer of an education unit is required to provide opportunities for Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.

(2) Every organizer of an education unit is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.

(3) In the event that a Child victim of Violence experiences dropping out of school, the organizer of the education unit must coordinate with relevant agencies.

a. promotive;

b. preventive;

c. curative; and

d. rehabilitative.

(3) Women and children victims of acts of Violence and children in conflict with the law have the right to health services free of charge, including:

a. medical services;

b. medicolegal services;

c. psychosocial counseling; and

Article 67

(1) In order to prevent violations of women's rights, the community:

d. supervises the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection organized by the City Government

General

CHAPTER X SANCTIONS

Article 73

(1) Any person who deliberately fails to provide protection to women and Children resulting in violence, fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

(2) If an official appointed to provide protection fails to carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

(3) UPT managers who carry out service duties but violate service principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable mechanism.

(4) Private parties that carry out Public services and fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities in accordance with this regulation shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 65

Service efforts carried out by the City Government for child victims of acts of Violence as referred to in Article 42 through Article 64 shall apply mutatis mutandis to service efforts for child victims of acts of Violence.

Part Two Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women and Children

Article 17

In order to prevent acts of Violence against women and children, the City Government:

a. conducts socialization regarding the prevention of Violence against women and children by optimizing the role of customary institutions, Education, culture, religion and community organizations;

b. builds networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, universities and various non-governmental organizations that work and/or care for women and children victims of Violence;

c. provides public facilities that are comfortable and safe for women and children; and

d. establishes an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment P2TP2A formed by decree of the Mayor and provides a Secretariat for the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment.

Part Five Law Enforcement and Legal Aid

Article 27

(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 19 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in the context of handling cases of acts of Violence against women and children, especially to provide sanctions against perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 25

(1) The City Government may provide safe houses for women and children victims of acts of Violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and children victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for women and children victims of acts of Violence who require a safe house include:

a. their life is threatened;

b. receiving rejection from family or community;

c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or

d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have sensitivity to women's empowerment and child protection and/or gender awareness, consisting of:

a. social workers/volunteers;

b. security officers; and/or

c. community leaders.

(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 46

(1) Every Child has the right to obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.

(2) Every Child has the right to receive Protection in education units from sexual crimes and Violence committed by educators, education personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.

Article 45

(1) Every organizer of an education unit is required to provide opportunities for Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.

(2) Every organizer of an education unit is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.

(3) In the event that a Child victim of Violence experiences dropping out of school, the organizer of the education unit must coordinate with relevant agencies.

Part Three Health Rehabilitation

Article 22

(1) Health rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter b constitutes efforts that include aspects of:

a. promotive;

b. preventive;

c. curative; and

d. rehabilitative.

(2) Health rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours, of quality and conducted in accordance with health service standards.

(3) Women and children victims of acts of Violence and children in conflict with the law have the right to health services free of charge, including:

a. medical services;

b. medicolegal services;

c. psychosocial counseling; and

d. visum.

(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementing health services as referred to in paragraph (3) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 30

(1) Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women and children victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

(2) Social reintegration is intended so that:

a. women and children victims of acts of Violence can resume their social life; and

b. women and children victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life.

(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

The City Government implements repatriation and social reintegration of women and children victims of acts of Violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

(1) Repatriation is intended to return women and children victims of acts of Violence to their region of origin.

(2) Repatriation of women and children victims of acts of violence is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

Part Two Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women and Children

Article 17

In order to prevent acts of Violence against women and children, the City Government:

a. conducts socialization regarding the prevention of Violence against women and children by optimizing the role of customary institutions, Education, culture, religion and community organizations;

b. builds networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, universities and various non-governmental organizations that work and/or care for women and children victims of Violence;

c. provides public facilities that are comfortable and safe for women and children; and

d. establishes an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment P2TP2A formed by decree of the Mayor and provides a Secretariat for the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment.

Article 25

(1) The City Government may provide safe houses for women and children victims of acts of Violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and children victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for women and children victims of acts of Violence who require a safe house include:

a. their life is threatened;

b. receiving rejection from family or community;

c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or

d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have sensitivity to women's empowerment and child protection and/or gender awareness, consisting of:

a. social workers/volunteers;

b. security officers; and/or

c. community leaders.

Article 21

(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of:

b. families;

c. communities; and/or

(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:

a. directly;

b. by telephone; and/or

c. by letter.

Article 73

(1) Any person who deliberately fails to provide protection to women and Children resulting in violence, fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

(2) If an official appointed to provide protection fails to carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

(3) UPT managers who carry out service duties but violate service principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable mechanism.

(4) Private parties that carry out Public services and fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities in accordance with this regulation shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 30

(1) Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women and children victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

(2) Social reintegration is intended so that:

a. women and children victims of acts of Violence can resume their social life; and

b. women and children victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life.

(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities. 36. Community Organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila. 37. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 38. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 39. Article 30

(1) Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women and children victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

(2) Social reintegration is intended so that:

a. women and children victims of acts of Violence can resume their social life; and

b. women and children victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life.

(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

Part Six Facilitation of the Juvenile Justice System

Article 58

(1) Facilitation of the juvenile justice system includes criminal and civil justice.

(2) Facilitation of the criminal justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:

a. provision of companions or Child volunteers during examination by investigators;

b. provision of legal aid and psychologist services;

c. involving members/investigators of the local police in efforts to prevent criminal acts committed by Children as well as Children as victims;

d. realizing a restorative justice process for Children in conflict with the law; and

e. rehabilitation and social reintegration services.

(3) Fulfillment of Children's rights in the civil justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) includes the provision and delivery of consultation and legal aid services during the judicial process.

(4) In facilitating the juvenile justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), the authorized RG is the RG with authority over women and Child empowerment and Protection and has the obligation to accompany child victims and perpetrators in police, prosecution and court examinations.

Article 25

(1) The City Government may provide safe houses for women and children victims of acts of Violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and children victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for women and children victims of acts of Violence who require a safe house include:

a. their life is threatened;

b. receiving rejection from family or community;

c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or

d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have sensitivity to women's empowerment and child protection and/or gender awareness, consisting of:

a. social workers/volunteers;

b. security officers; and/or

c. community leaders.

(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Part Two Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women and Children

Article 17

In order to prevent acts of Violence against women and children, the City Government:

a. conducts socialization regarding the prevention of Violence against women and children by optimizing the role of customary institutions, Education, culture, religion and community organizations;

b. builds networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, universities and various non-governmental organizations that work and/or care for women and children victims of Violence;

c. provides public facilities that are comfortable and safe for women and children; and

d. establishes an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment P2TP2A formed by decree of the Mayor and provides a Secretariat for the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment.

Article 65

Service efforts carried out by the City Government for child victims of acts of Violence as referred to in Article 42 through Article 64 shall apply mutatis mutandis to service efforts for child victims of acts of Violence.

Article 37

Counseling as referred to in Article 35 letter b includes:

a. conducting outreach on improving the quality of life of women and children; and

b. conducting premarital counseling.

Part Four Health and Social

Article 48

(1) The City Government is required to organize comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the womb.

(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services; and

b. exemption from cost burdens for Children with malnutrition, Children with disabilities, Children with special needs, Children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, Children victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, Children who are victims of Violence, and Children victims of human trafficking.

(3) The City Government, community, family and parents are required to ensure that Children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Part Six Repatriation and Social Reintegration

Article 29

(1) Repatriation is intended to return women and children victims of acts of Violence to their region of origin.

(2) Repatriation of women and children victims of acts of violence is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

Article 31

The City Government implements repatriation and social reintegration of women and children victims of acts of Violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

Part Five Law Enforcement and Legal Aid

Article 27

(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 19 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in the context of handling cases of acts of Violence against women and children, especially to provide sanctions against perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 21

(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of:

a. victims;

b. families;

c. communities; and/or

d. community organizations in the field of Protection of women and children.

(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:

a. directly;

b. by telephone; and/or

c. by letter.

(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency responsible for the Protection of Women and children, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20, are also authorized to conduct Assistance in handling victims of acts of Violence against women and children obtained through other information.

(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 68

a. protecting women and children from conflict and domestic Violence that degrades human dignity;

b. providing equal opportunities for women and children to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural affairs; and

c. preventing violations of the rights of women and children in the household.

Part Three Health Rehabilitation

Article 22

(1) Health rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter b constitutes efforts that include aspects of:

a. promotive;

b. preventive;

c. curative; and

d. rehabilitative.

(2) Health rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours, of quality and conducted in accordance with health service standards.

(3) Women and children victims of acts of Violence and children in conflict with the law have the right to health services free of charge, including:

a. medical services;

b. medicolegal services;

c. psychosocial counseling; and

d. visum.

(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementing health services as referred to in paragraph (3) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 25

(1) The City Government may provide safe houses for women and children victims of acts of Violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and children victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for women and children victims of acts of Violence who require a safe house include:

a. their life is threatened;

b. receiving rejection from family or community;

c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or

d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have sensitivity to women's empowerment and child protection and/or gender awareness, consisting of:

a. social workers/volunteers;

b. security officers; and/or

c. community leaders.

(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 72

Financing for the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection programs and activities is sourced from:

a. regional revenue and expenditure budget; and

b. other legitimate sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 27. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 28. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 29. c. supervise the law enforcement process for cases of violations of the rights of women and Children.

(2) The community, parents and family are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and Children.

CHAPTER X SANCTIONS

Article 73

(4) Private parties that carry out Public services and fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities in accordance with this regulation shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 21

(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of:

a. victims;

b. families;

c. communities; and/or

d. community organizations in the field of Protection of women and children.

(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:

a. directly;

b. by telephone; and/or

c. by letter.

Article 67

(1) In order to prevent violations of women's rights, the community:

a. monitors various conditions occurring in their environment that may lead to violations of women's rights;

b. increases awareness of violations of women's rights;

c. strengthens the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and

d. supervises the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection organized by the City Government

through a mechanism for conveying aspirations to the Mayor or the Regional House of Representatives.

(2) In order to prevent violations of Children's rights, the community:

a. monitors various conditions occurring in their environment that lead to violations of Children's rights;

b. increases awareness of violations of Children's rights; and

c. strengthens the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and prevents early marriage.

a. protecting women and children from conflict and domestic Violence that degrades human dignity;

b. providing equal opportunities for women and children to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural affairs; and

c. preventing violations of the rights of women and children in the household.

a. conducting socialization to increase women's legal knowledge and awareness;

b. mapping and reviewing gender-biased policies; and

c. involving women's organizations in the process of drafting and discussing Regional legal products related to women's participation.

Article 25

(1) The City Government may provide safe houses for women and children victims of acts of Violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and children victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for women and children victims of acts of Violence who require a safe house include:

a. their life is threatened;

b. receiving rejection from family or community;

c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or

d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have sensitivity to women's empowerment and child protection and/or gender awareness, consisting of:

a. social workers/volunteers;

b. security officers; and/or

c. community leaders.

a. promotive;

b. preventive;

c. curative; and

d. rehabilitative.

(2) Health rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours, of quality and conducted in accordance with health service standards.

(3) Women and children victims of acts of Violence and children in conflict with the law have the right to health services free of charge, including:

a. medical services;

b. medicolegal services;

c. psychosocial counseling; and

d. visum.

The City Government implements repatriation and social reintegration of women and children victims of acts of Violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

a. women and children victims of acts of Violence can resume their social life; and

CHAPTER II

IMPROVEMENT OF QUALITY OF LIFE OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part One

General

Article 5

(1) In order to improve the quality of life of women and children, the City Government is responsible for:

a. respecting and guaranteeing the rights of women and children without discrimination in accordance with human dignity;

b. enhancing Women's Empowerment and child protection in terms of role, quality and capacity in the fields of:

1. politics;

2. law;

3. social;

4. economy; and

5. culture.

c. strengthening and developing service provider institutions for Women's Empowerment and child protection in the City.

(2) The responsibility of the City Government in efforts to improve the quality of life of women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by Regional Apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.

Part Four Health and Social

Article 48

(1) The City Government is required to organize comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the womb.

(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services; and

b. exemption from cost burdens for Children with malnutrition, Children with disabilities, Children with special needs, Children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, Children victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, Children who are victims of Violence, and Children victims of human trafficking.

(3) The City Government, community, family and parents are required to ensure that Children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Part Two Parents and/or Family

Article 68

The family in efforts to Protect women's rights plays a role in:

a. protecting women and children from conflict and domestic Violence that degrades human dignity;

b. providing equal opportunities for women and children to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural affairs; and

c. preventing violations of the rights of women and children in the household.

Article 67

(1) In order to prevent violations of women's rights, the community:

a. monitors various conditions occurring in their environment that may lead to violations of women's rights;

b. increases awareness of violations of women's rights;

c. strengthens the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and

d. supervises the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection organized by the City Government

through a mechanism for conveying aspirations to the Mayor or the Regional House of Representatives.

(2) In order to prevent violations of Children's rights, the community:

a. monitors various conditions occurring in their environment that lead to violations of Children's rights;

b. increases awareness of violations of Children's rights; and

c. strengthens the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and prevents early marriage.

CHAPTER VII COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION, AND PARENTS AND/OR FAMILY

Part One Community

Article 66

(1) Community participation in efforts to Protect women and Children:

a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and Children;

b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and Children to the competent authorities; and

c. supervise the law enforcement process for cases of violations of the rights of women and Children.

(2) The community, parents and family are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and Children.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

CHAPTER X SANCTIONS

Article 73

(1) Any person who deliberately fails to provide protection to women and Children resulting in violence, fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

(2) If an official appointed to provide protection fails to carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

(3) UPT managers who carry out service duties but violate service principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable mechanism.

(4) Private parties that carry out Public services and fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities in accordance with this regulation shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 25

(1) The City Government may provide safe houses for women and children victims of acts of Violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and children victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for women and children victims of acts of Violence who require a safe house include:

a. their life is threatened;

b. receiving rejection from family or community;

c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or

d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have sensitivity to women's empowerment and child protection and/or gender awareness, consisting of:

a. social workers/volunteers;

b. security officers; and/or

c. community leaders.

(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Mayor Regulation.
