c. strengthens the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and

d. supervises the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection organized by the City Government

through a mechanism for conveying aspirations to the Mayor or the Regional House of Representatives.

(2) In order to prevent violations of Children's rights, the community:

a. monitors various conditions occurring in their environment that lead to violations of Children's rights;

b. increases awareness of violations of Children's rights; and

c. strengthens the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and prevents early marriage.

CHAPTER II

IMPROVEMENT OF QUALITY OF LIFE OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part One

General

Article 5

(1) In order to improve the quality of life of women and children, the City Government is responsible for:

a. respecting and guaranteeing the rights of women and children without discrimination in accordance with human dignity;

b. enhancing Women's Empowerment and child protection in terms of role, quality and capacity in the fields of:

1. politics;

2. law;

3. social;

4. economy; and

5. culture.

c. strengthening and developing service provider institutions for Women's Empowerment and child protection in the City.

(2) The responsibility of the City Government in efforts to improve the quality of life of women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by Regional Apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.

Article 17

a. conducts socialization regarding the prevention of Violence against women and children by optimizing the role of customary institutions, Education, culture, religion and community organizations;

b. builds networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, universities and various non-governmental organizations that work and/or care for women and children victims of Violence;

c. provides public facilities that are comfortable and safe for women and children; and

d. establishes an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment P2TP2A formed by decree of the Mayor and provides a Secretariat for the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment.

CHAPTER VII COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION, AND PARENTS AND/OR FAMILY

Part One Community

Article 66

a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and Children;

b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and Children to the competent authorities; and

c. supervise the law enforcement process for cases of violations of the rights of women and Children.

(2) The community, parents and family are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and Children.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Part Four Health and Social

Article 48

(1) The City Government is required to organize comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the womb.

(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services; and

b. exemption from cost burdens for Children with malnutrition, Children with disabilities, Children with special needs, Children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, Children victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, Children who are victims of Violence, and Children victims of human trafficking.

(3) The City Government, community, family and parents are required to ensure that Children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Article 71

(1) Supervision of the implementation of women's empowerment and Child Protection as regulated in this Regional Regulation is carried out by a Supervisory institution specifically established for that purpose.

(2) In carrying out supervision, the Institution referred to is authorized to recommend cases to law enforcement officials, government agencies and other community institutions as regulated in the Law.

(3) Recommendations submitted must be followed up by law enforcement officials, government agencies, community institutions and other related individuals.

(1) In order to prevent violations of women's rights, the community:

a. monitors various conditions occurring in their environment that may lead to violations of women's rights;

b. increases awareness of violations of women's rights;

c. strengthens the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and

d. supervises the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection organized by the City Government

through a mechanism for conveying aspirations to the Mayor or the Regional House of Representatives.

(2) In order to prevent violations of Children's rights, the community:

a. monitors various conditions occurring in their environment that lead to violations of Children's rights;

b. increases awareness of violations of Children's rights; and

c. strengthens the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and prevents early marriage.

Article 63

In carrying out its duties, the CFC Task Force may coordinate and cooperate with other institutions that provide Child Protection services.

Article 10

(1) The Technical Team as referred to in Article 9 letter j shall consist of officials who understand gender responsive budget analysis as well as Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

(2) The Regional Women's Empowerment and Child Protection regional action plan as referred to in Article 9 letter k shall contain:

a. women's empowerment and child protection in laws and regulations in the City;

b. women's empowerment and child protection in the development cycle in the City;

c. institutional strengthening of women's empowerment and child protection in the City; and

d. strengthening community participation in the City.

Article 21

(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of:

a. victims;

b. families;

c. communities; and/or

d. community organizations in the field of Protection of women and children.

(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:

a. directly;

b. by telephone; and/or

c. by letter.

(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency responsible for the Protection of Women and children, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20, are also authorized to conduct Assistance in handling victims of acts of Violence against women and children obtained through other information.

(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Part Seven Children's Forum

Article 59

(1) In organizing the fulfillment of Children's rights to express opinions and participate, the City Government shall facilitate the establishment of a Children's Forum.

(2) The Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) represents Children in the City, both representing Children's geographic domicile, components of Children's socio-cultural groups and Children's educational background.

(3) In every formulation of policies related to Children, the City Government must consider and accommodate the opinions of Children conveyed through the Children's participation Forum.

(4) Further provisions regarding the establishment of the Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) through paragraph (3) shall be stipulated by Mayor Regulation.

Part Six Facilitation of the Juvenile Justice System

Article 58

(1) Facilitation of the juvenile justice system includes criminal and civil justice.

(2) Facilitation of the criminal justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:

a. provision of companions or Child volunteers during examination by investigators;

b. provision of legal aid and psychologist services;

c. involving members/investigators of the local police in efforts to prevent criminal acts committed by Children as well as Children as victims;

d. realizing a restorative justice process for Children in conflict with the law; and

e. rehabilitation and social reintegration services.

(3) Fulfillment of Children's rights in the civil justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) includes the provision and delivery of consultation and legal aid services during the judicial process.

(4) In facilitating the juvenile justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), the authorized RG is the RG with authority over women and Child empowerment and Protection and has the obligation to accompany child victims and perpetrators in police, prosecution and court examinations.

Article 25

(1) The City Government may provide safe houses for women and children victims of acts of Violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and children victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for women and children victims of acts of Violence who require a safe house include:

a. their life is threatened;

b. receiving rejection from family or community;

c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or

d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have sensitivity to women's empowerment and child protection and/or gender awareness, consisting of:

a. social workers/volunteers;

b. security officers; and/or

c. community leaders.

(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Communication, information and education as referred to in Article 39 letter a constitutes communication activities to increase knowledge and improve the attitudes and behavior of families and communities in population and family planning Programs.

Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 33. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 35. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities. 36. Community Organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the objectives of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila. 37. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 38. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 39. Customs are eternal and hereditary codes of conduct from one generation to the next generation as heritage, so that they are strongly integrated with the behavioral patterns of society.

CHAPTER X SANCTIONS

Article 73

(1) Any person who deliberately fails to provide protection to women and Children resulting in violence, fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

(2) If an official appointed to provide protection fails to carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

(3) UPT managers who carry out service duties but violate service principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable mechanism.

(4) Private parties that carry out Public services and fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities in accordance with this regulation shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

(1) The City Government may provide safe houses for women and children victims of acts of Violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and children victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for women and children victims of acts of Violence who require a safe house include:

a. their life is threatened;

b. receiving rejection from family or community;

c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or

d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have sensitivity to women's empowerment and child protection and/or gender awareness, consisting of:

a. social workers/volunteers;

b. security officers; and/or

c. community leaders.

(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Part Five Law Enforcement and Legal Aid

Article 27

(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 19 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in the context of handling cases of acts of Violence against women and children, especially to provide sanctions against perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 30

(1) Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women and children victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

(2) Social reintegration is intended so that:

a. women and children victims of acts of Violence can resume their social life; and

b. women and children victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life.

(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

Article 31

The City Government implements repatriation and social reintegration of women and children victims of acts of Violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VII COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION, AND PARENTS AND/OR FAMILY

Part One Community

Article 66

(1) Community participation in efforts to Protect women and Children:

a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and Children;

b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and Children to the competent authorities; and

c. supervise the law enforcement process for cases of violations of the rights of women and Children.

(2) The community, parents and family are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and Children.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 71

(1) Supervision of the implementation of women's empowerment and Child Protection as regulated in this Regional Regulation is carried out by a Supervisory institution specifically established for that purpose.

(2) In carrying out supervision, the Institution referred to is authorized to recommend cases to law enforcement officials, government agencies and other community institutions as regulated in the Law.

(3) Recommendations submitted must be followed up by law enforcement officials, government agencies, community institutions and other related individuals.

Article 21

(1) Complaints of acts of Violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of:

a. victims;

b. families;

c. communities; and/or

d. community organizations in the field of Protection of women and children.

(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:

a. directly;

b. by telephone; and/or

c. by letter.

(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency responsible for the Protection of Women and children, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 20, are also authorized to conduct Assistance in handling victims of acts of Violence against women and children obtained through other information.

(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Part Six Facilitation of the Juvenile Justice System

Article 58

(1) Facilitation of the juvenile justice system includes criminal and civil justice.

(2) Facilitation of the criminal justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:

a. provision of companions or Child volunteers during examination by investigators;

b. provision of legal aid and psychologist services;

c. involving members/investigators of the local police in efforts to prevent criminal acts committed by Children as well as Children as victims;

d. realizing a restorative justice process for Children in conflict with the law; and

e. rehabilitation and social reintegration services.

(3) Fulfillment of Children's rights in the civil justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) includes the provision and delivery of consultation and legal aid services during the judicial process.

(4) In facilitating the juvenile justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), the authorized RG is the RG with authority over women and Child empowerment and Protection and has the obligation to accompany child victims and perpetrators in police, prosecution and court examinations.

Part Six Repatriation and Social Reintegration

Article 29

(1) Repatriation is intended to return women and children victims of acts of Violence to their region of origin.

(2) Repatriation of women and children victims of acts of violence is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

Article 17

In order to prevent acts of Violence against women and children, the City Government:

a. conducts socialization regarding the prevention of Violence against women and children by optimizing the role of customary institutions, Education, culture, religion and community organizations;

b. builds networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, universities and various non-governmental organizations that work and/or care for women and children victims of Violence;

c. provides public facilities that are comfortable and safe for women and children; and

d. establishes an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment P2TP2A formed by decree of the Mayor and provides a Secretariat for the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment.

Article 48

Part Seven Employment Protection

Article 32

(1) Employers who employ women are obliged to maintain decency, safety and security while at the workplace.

(2) Employers are obliged to place female workers in places that are safe for women's reproductive health.

(3) Employers are obliged to fulfill the rights of female workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(4) Employers are obliged to provide special breastfeeding facilities at their company.

Article 33

(1) Female workers/laborers who are less than 18 (eighteen) years old are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.

(2) Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant female workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy.

(3) Employers who employ female workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB, are obliged to:

a. provide nutritious food and drinks; and

b. maintain Employers are obliged to provide shuttle transportation for female workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB until 05.00 WIB.

Part Two Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women and Children

Article 17

In order to prevent acts of Violence against women and children, the City Government:

a. conducts socialization regarding the prevention of Violence against women and children by optimizing the role of customary institutions, Education, culture, religion and community organizations;

b. builds networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, universities and various non-governmental organizations that work and/or care for women and children victims of Violence;

c. provides public facilities that are comfortable and safe for women and children; and

d. establishes an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment P2TP2A formed by decree of the Mayor and provides a Secretariat for the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment.

Part Five Law Enforcement and Legal Aid

Article 27

(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 19 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in the context of handling cases of acts of Violence against women and children, especially to provide sanctions against perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Part Three Health Rehabilitation

Article 22

(1) Health rehabilitation as referred to in Article 19 letter b constitutes efforts that include aspects of:

a. promotive;

b. preventive;

c. curative; and

d. rehabilitative.

(2) Health rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours, of quality and conducted in accordance with health service standards.

(3) Women and children victims of acts of Violence and children in conflict with the law have the right to health services free of charge, including:

a. medical services;

b. medicolegal services;

c. psychosocial counseling; and

d. visum.

(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementing health services as referred to in paragraph (3) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

IMPROVEMENT OF FAMILY QUALITY

Article 34

(1) In order to improve the quality of family life, the City Government is responsible for:

a. making efforts to improve family quality to realize gender equality and Children's rights;

b. providing services for families in realizing gender equality and Children's rights; and

c. strengthening and developing institutions providing family quality improvement services in the City.

(2) The City Government's responsibility in efforts to improve family quality as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by Regional Apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.

Article 25

(1) The City Government may provide safe houses for women and children victims of acts of Violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and children victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for women and children victims of acts of Violence who require a safe house include:

a. their life is threatened;

b. receiving rejection from family or community;

c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or

d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have sensitivity to women's empowerment and child protection and/or gender awareness, consisting of:

a. social workers/volunteers;

b. security officers; and/or

c. community leaders.

(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

CHAPTER X SANCTIONS

Article 73

(1) Any person who deliberately fails to provide protection to women and Children resulting in violence, fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

(2) If an official appointed to provide protection fails to carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

(3) UPT managers who carry out service duties but violate service principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable mechanism.

(4) Private parties that carry out Public services and fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities in accordance with this regulation shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 58

a. provision of companions or Child volunteers during examination by investigators;

b. provision of legal aid and psychologist services;

c. involving members/investigators of the local police in efforts to prevent criminal acts committed by Children as well as Children as victims;

d. realizing a restorative justice process for Children in conflict with the law; and

c. preventing violations of the rights of women and children in the household.

14. Women's Empowerment is an effort of Protection, strengthening of human rights, improvement of quality of life, and enhancement of women's participation in development. 15. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb and is not married. 17. Child-Friendly City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a City that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights

21. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 25. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 26. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 27. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 28. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 29. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 31. IMPROVEMENT OF FAMILY QUALITY

Article 34

(1) In order to improve the quality of family life, the City Government is responsible for:

a. making efforts to improve family quality to realize gender equality and Children's rights;

b. providing services for families in realizing gender equality and Children's rights; and

c. strengthening and developing institutions providing family quality improvement services in the City.

(2) The City Government's responsibility in efforts to improve family quality as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by Regional Apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.

Article 10

(1) The Technical Team as referred to in Article 9 letter j shall consist of officials who understand gender responsive budget analysis as well as Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

(2) The Regional Women's Empowerment and Child Protection regional action plan as referred to in Article 9 letter k shall contain:

a. women's empowerment and child protection in laws and regulations in the City;

b. women's empowerment and child protection in the development cycle in the City;

c. institutional strengthening of women's empowerment and child protection in the City; and

d. strengthening community participation in the City.

Part Four Health and Social

Article 48

(1) The City Government is required to organize comprehensive health services for Children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the womb.

(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services; and

b. exemption from cost burdens for Children with malnutrition, Children with disabilities, Children with special needs, Children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, Children victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, Children who are victims of Violence, and Children victims of human trafficking.

(3) The City Government, community, family and parents are required to ensure that Children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Part Seven Children's Forum

Article 59

(1) In organizing the fulfillment of Children's rights to express opinions and participate, the City Government shall facilitate the establishment of a Children's Forum.

(2) The Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) represents Children in the City, both representing Children's geographic domicile, components of Children's socio-cultural groups and Children's educational background.

(3) In every formulation of policies related to Children, the City Government must consider and accommodate the opinions of Children conveyed through the Children's participation Forum.

(4) Further provisions regarding the establishment of the Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) through paragraph (3) shall be stipulated by Mayor Regulation.

Part Three  Establishment of Working Group  for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the City

Article 8

(1) In an effort to accelerate the institutionalization of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in all Regional Apparatus, a working group for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the City shall be established.

(2) Members of the working group for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are all heads/leaders of Regional Apparatus.

(3) The Mayor shall appoint the Head of the Regional Apparatus that handles Women's Empowerment duties as Chairman of the Working Group and Head of the Secretariat of the Regional Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Working Group.

(4) The establishment of the City Women's Empowerment and Child Protection working group shall be stipulated by Mayor's Decree.

Article 25

(1) The City Government may provide safe houses for women and children victims of acts of Violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and children victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for women and children victims of acts of Violence who require a safe house include:

a. their life is threatened;

b. receiving rejection from family or community;

c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or

d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have sensitivity to women's empowerment and child protection and/or gender awareness, consisting of:

a. social workers/volunteers;

b. security officers; and/or

c. community leaders.

(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 67

(1) In order to prevent violations of women's rights, the community:

a. monitors various conditions occurring in their environment that may lead to violations of women's rights;

b. increases awareness of violations of women's rights;

c. strengthens the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and

d. supervises the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection organized by the City Government

through a mechanism for conveying aspirations to the Mayor or the Regional House of Representatives.

(2) In order to prevent violations of Children's rights, the community:

a. monitors various conditions occurring in their environment that lead to violations of Children's rights;

b. increases awareness of violations of Children's rights; and

c. strengthens the role of community organizations, religious organizations and the family environment; and prevents early marriage.

Part Two Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women and Children

Article 17

In order to prevent acts of Violence against women and children, the City Government:

a. conducts socialization regarding the prevention of Violence against women and children by optimizing the role of customary institutions, Education, culture, religion and community organizations;

b. builds networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, universities and various non-governmental organizations that work and/or care for women and children victims of Violence;

c. provides public facilities that are comfortable and safe for women and children; and

d. establishes an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment P2TP2A formed by decree of the Mayor and provides a Secretariat for the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment.

Part Two Parents and/or Family

Article 68

The family in efforts to Protect women's rights plays a role in:

a. protecting women and children from conflict and domestic Violence that degrades human dignity;

b. providing equal opportunities for women and children to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural affairs; and

c. preventing violations of the rights of women and children in the household.

Part Five Law Enforcement and Legal Aid

Article 27

(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 19 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in the context of handling cases of acts of Violence against women and children, especially to provide sanctions against perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 30

(1) Social reintegration is carried out in order to reunite women and children victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

(2) Social reintegration is intended so that:

a. women and children victims of acts of Violence can resume their social life; and

b. women and children victims of acts of Violence can have a decent life.

(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

CHAPTER VII COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION, AND PARENTS AND/OR FAMILY

Part One Community

Article 66

(1) Community participation in efforts to Protect women and Children:

a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and Children;

b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and Children to the competent authorities; and

c. supervise the law enforcement process for cases of violations of the rights of women and Children.

(2) The community, parents and family are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and Children.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

CHAPTER X SANCTIONS

Article 73

(1) Any person who deliberately fails to provide protection to women and Children resulting in violence, fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

(2) If an official appointed to provide protection fails to carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

(3) UPT managers who carry out service duties but violate service principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable mechanism.

(4) Private parties that carry out Public services and fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities in accordance with this regulation shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

a. women's empowerment and child protection in laws and regulations in the City;

b. women's empowerment and child protection in the development cycle in the City;

c. institutional strengthening of women's empowerment and child protection in the City; and

d. strengthening community participation in the City.

Part Six Repatriation and Social Reintegration

Article 29

(1) Repatriation is intended to return women and children victims of acts of Violence to their region of origin.

(2) Repatriation of women and children victims of acts of violence is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

Article 71

(1) Supervision of the implementation of women's empowerment and Child Protection as regulated in this Regional Regulation is carried out by a Supervisory institution specifically established for that purpose.

(2) In carrying out supervision, the Institution referred to is authorized to recommend cases to law enforcement officials, government agencies and other community institutions as regulated in the Law.

(3) Recommendations submitted must be followed up by law enforcement officials, government agencies, community institutions and other related individuals.

CHAPTER II

IMPROVEMENT OF QUALITY OF LIFE OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part One

General

Article 5

(1) In order to improve the quality of life of women and children, the City Government is responsible for:

a. respecting and guaranteeing the rights of women and children without discrimination in accordance with human dignity;

b. enhancing Women's Empowerment and child protection in terms of role, quality and capacity in the fields of:

1. politics;

2. law;

3. social;

4. economy; and

5. culture.

c. strengthening and developing service provider institutions for Women's Empowerment and child protection in the City.

(2) The responsibility of the City Government in efforts to improve the quality of life of women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by Regional Apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.

IMPROVEMENT OF FAMILY QUALITY

Article 34

(1) In order to improve the quality of family life, the City Government is responsible for:

a. making efforts to improve family quality to realize gender equality and Children's rights;

b. providing services for families in realizing gender equality and Children's rights; and

c. strengthening and developing institutions providing family quality improvement services in the City.

(2) The City Government's responsibility in efforts to improve family quality as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by Regional Apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.

Part Two Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women and Children

Article 17

In order to prevent acts of Violence against women and children, the City Government:

a. conducts socialization regarding the prevention of Violence against women and children by optimizing the role of customary institutions, Education, culture, religion and community organizations;

b. builds networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, government apparatus, universities and various non-governmental organizations that work and/or care for women and children victims of Violence;

c. provides public facilities that are comfortable and safe for women and children; and

d. establishes an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment P2TP2A formed by decree of the Mayor and provides a Secretariat for the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment.

Part Three  Establishment of Working Group  for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the City

Article 8

(1) In an effort to accelerate the institutionalization of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in all Regional Apparatus, a working group for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the City shall be established.

(2) Members of the working group for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection are all heads/leaders of Regional Apparatus.

(3) The Mayor shall appoint the Head of the Regional Apparatus that handles Women's Empowerment duties as Chairman of the Working Group and Head of the Secretariat of the Regional Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Working Group.

(4) The establishment of the City Women's Empowerment and Child Protection working group shall be stipulated by Mayor's Decree.

Part Five Law Enforcement and Legal Aid

Article 27

(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 19 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in the context of handling cases of acts of Violence against women and children, especially to provide sanctions against perpetrators and provide Protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Part Seven Children's Forum

Article 59

(1) In organizing the fulfillment of Children's rights to express opinions and participate, the City Government shall facilitate the establishment of a Children's Forum.

(2) The Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) represents Children in the City, both representing Children's geographic domicile, components of Children's socio-cultural groups and Children's educational background.

(3) In every formulation of policies related to Children, the City Government must consider and accommodate the opinions of Children conveyed through the Children's participation Forum.

(4) Further provisions regarding the establishment of the Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) through paragraph (3) shall be stipulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 25

(1) The City Government may provide safe houses for women and children victims of acts of Violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect women and children victims of acts of Violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for women and children victims of acts of Violence who require a safe house include:

a. their life is threatened;

b. receiving rejection from family or community;

c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or

d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

(5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have sensitivity to women's empowerment and child protection and/or gender awareness, consisting of:

a. social workers/volunteers;

b. security officers; and/or

c. community leaders.

(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Part Six Facilitation of the Juvenile Justice System

Article 58

(1) Facilitation of the juvenile justice system includes criminal and civil justice.

(2) Facilitation of the criminal justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:

a. provision of companions or Child volunteers during examination by investigators;

b. provision of legal aid and psychologist services;

c. involving members/investigators of the local police in efforts to prevent criminal acts committed by Children as well as Children as victims;

d. realizing a restorative justice process for Children in conflict with the law; and

e. rehabilitation and social reintegration services.

(3) Fulfillment of Children's rights in the civil justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) includes the provision and delivery of consultation and legal aid services during the judicial process.

(4) In facilitating the juvenile justice system as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), the authorized RG is the RG with authority over women and Child empowerment and Protection and has the obligation to accompany child victims and perpetrators in police, prosecution and court examinations.
